title: Negative Wick defect is first order while fixed-moment Fisher excess is second order near the profiled Gaussian

fixed_moment_tangent.orthogonality: At the interior K1572 Gaussian optimum, the Hamiltonian residual is orthogonal to normalization, mean and covariance Gaussian tangents because those parameters were already varied in the Gaussian minimization.
fixed_moment_tangent.exact_moment_correction: Project a bounded smooth approximation to the negative residual away from constant, linear and quadratic Gaussian statistics, then use the local Gaussian exponential family to restore normalization, mean and covariance exactly; the correction begins at second order.
fixed_moment_tangent.fisher_order: K1533 Gaussian extremality and smoothness on the exact fixed-moment manifold give F(rho_epsilon)-F(G_N)=O(epsilon^2).
fixed_moment_tangent.defect_order: The total first variation is strictly negative by K1581 and the free first variation vanishes, so K1534's integrated Wick defect equals -c_N epsilon+O(epsilon^2) with c_N>0.
fixed_moment_tangent.excluded_linear_compensation: No neighborhood admits F(rho)-F(G_N)>=c[-D(rho)]_+ with fixed c>0: the left side is quadratic and the right side linear along the constructed curve.
fixed_moment_tangent.scope_guard: This excludes only local linear Fisher compensation at fixed cutoff. It does not exclude quadratic, cutoff-dependent or global nonlinear compensation and supplies no unrestricted leading coefficient or bounded-error estimate.
